subject: Environmental Education and Urban Meadow Initiatives
overview: The committee discussed Medford Public Schools' environmental science programs and proposed initiatives for urban meadows and non-toxic rodent control. New members were introduced and the committee coordinated upcoming community events, including the Harvest Your Energy Festival.

items.title: Medford Public Schools Science Initiatives
items.summary: Science Director Rocco Cieri detailed student projects involving marbled salamander reintroduction, Blanding’s turtle growth, and a new sustainability think tank pilot program. The committee discussed opportunities for student ambassadors to participate in city environmental meetings and festivals.

items.title: New Member Introductions
items.summary: New members Sarah Singh, Dan, and Lois Grossman introduced themselves, highlighting interests in rewilding, renewable energy markets, and pollinator gardens.

items.title: Planning Office Updates
items.summary: The committee received updates on a regional webinar for resilient building guidelines and a rain barrel distribution event scheduled for May 10. Potential in-person or outdoor meeting formats for the summer were also discussed.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Administrative Business
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the March 6 meeting. The chair announced an upcoming meeting with the Mayor on April 27 to discuss committee priorities.

items.title: Community Events and Reforestation Bill
items.summary: Lauretta James provided updates on the Harvest Your Energy Festival and Circle the Square, and discussed a legislative briefing for the state Municipal Reforestation Bill. The committee reviewed the progress of a proposed local tree ordinance regarding public and private tree canopy protections.

items.title: Rodent Control and Rodenticide Alternatives
items.summary: Following the poisoning deaths of local bald eagles, the committee proposed a public education meeting to promote non-toxic rodent control methods like carbon dioxide treatments and birth control. Members discussed collaborating with the Health Department to advertise alternatives to poisons that harm natural predators.

items.title: Urban Meadows Presentation
items.summary: The chair presented the benefits of urban meadows for biodiversity and climate resilience, outlining steps to establish native plant areas on city and private land. The committee explored ways to incentivize meadow creation for residents and require green space in new development projects.

items.title: Public Comment: Invasive Species and Solar Panels
items.summary: Members discussed concerns regarding tree removal for solar panel installations and addressed a resident's inquiry about managing invasive Japanese knotweed without chemicals.
